out: Prison Link Cymru warns that some ex-offenders are living rough for up to a year before finding suitable accommodation, while charity workers argue that investment in housing would be more cost-effective than re-incarcerating homeless repeat offenders. The Welsh Government maintains that more people are receiving help with housing issues than ever before, despite recent legislative changes that removed priority status for prison leavers.

Police executed searches in the Waterfront Park and Colonsay View areas, recovering three firearms, ammunition, and a significant amount of cash. A 26-year-old man who was arrested during the operation appeared at Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday to face charges.

Four young people in Chicago have been charged with hate crimes, aggravated kidnapping, and battery after allegedly torturing an 18-year-old white man with disabilities during a multi-day captivity. A judge denied their bail, condemning their actions as lacking any sense of decency. The victim was found on January 3 after being forced to endure dehum human treatment, including being made to drink toilet water and kissing the floor. The case has drawn significant public attention, with an online fundraiser for the victim already raising $51,000.

The 48-year-old former Arsenal goalkeeper has been with Reading for four years, serving as youth academy director since 2000 and as director of football since 2003. A West Brom statement highlighted his key role in helping the Championship club achieve promotion to the Premier League in both 2006 and 2012.

A study published in the journal *Cell* suggests that a "fasting-mimicking diet" can reverse symptoms of diabetes in mice by regenerating insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. The diet involves five days of restricted calorie intake followed by 25 days of normal eating, which appears to "reboot" the body and reprogram cells without genetic alteration. While researchers describe the findings as potentially exciting for future treatments, they caution against self-prescribing such extreme dietary regimns without medical supervision.

France's Essilor and Italy's Luxottica, the world's leading lens and frame manufacturers, proposed a merger to create the industry behemoth EssilorLuxottica, which would control the entire supply chain from manufacturing to retail. The deal has sparked significant concern among optometrists and industry insiders, who argue that the combined entity’s overwhelming market power could reduce consumer choice, stifle competition, and ultimately lower product quality. While the companies claim the merger will drive innovation and synergies, critics warn it could effectively monopolate the high-end eyewear market and squeeze out independent competitors.

Olympic silver medallist Rachel Hoovenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and lacking regard for athlete welfare, as she becomes the latest high-profile cyclist to criticize the organization's "win-at-all-costs" culture. A leaked draft report has vindicated her claims by admitting that British Cycling "sanitised" its own investigation into past misconduct and failed to prioritize staff wellbeing. British Cycling has since acknowledged these governance failings and implemented a 39-point action plan to address the cultural shortcomings within the World Class Programme.

Kareem Badr and his partners successfully turned around a struggling comedy club in Austin, by leveraging Badr's computer science background to optimize operations and expanding their premises. The Hideout has since grown to employ about 25 workers and allow Badr to quit his day job. The success of the Hideout reflects a broader national trend of rising enthusiasm for comedy clubs in the US, driven by younger audiences and the industry's ability to generate revenue through both entertainment and alcohol sales.

BT’s shares surged 3% in early trading after regulators determined that a forced breakup of the company would be delayed by practical obstacles, including complications with land deals and a massive, government-backed pension scheme. Ofcom plans to enforce separation through new governance structures for Openreach, such as distinct board duties and articles of association, rather than a full split. However, this approach risks future conflicts with BT’s ownership and could ultimately lead to a court battle if the details prove too restrictive for the company.

Brendan Rodgers is preparing for his first Old Firm derby as Rangers manager, looking to replicate his team's dominant performance from last month when they beat Celtic 5-1. Rodgers emphasized that his primary focus is on maintaining a high performance level and imposing his team's style of play to secure a victory in the Scottish Cup semi-final. While acknowledging the difficulty of achieving a domestic treble, he stated that winning this first trophy is the club's immediate priority.

Queen's University has announced a reduction of over 1,000 undergraduate places and staff cuts starting in September 2015, as a response to an £8m reduction in government subsidy. The university aims to balance its budget by focusing on growth areas, though Vice-Chancellor Patrick Johnston warned that these cuts could damage the institution's reputation and the local economy. Education Minister Stephen Farry echoed these concerns, stating that defunding higher education skills development is counterproductive to economic growth.

East Sussex NHS Trust has apologized after an administrative error by an external printing company resulted in approximately 850 patients receiving incorrect cancer information leaflets instead of their appointment letters. The trust attributed the mix-up to a coding mistake made in March, which inadvertently included urgent cancer symptom materials with standard appointment correspondence. The trust has since contacted all affected individuals to apologize and clarify the situation.

Labour MPs are preparing for a crucial vote on the Brexit bill, while Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell warned that frontbenchers who defy the party whip will be required to resign. The party aims to secure amendments regarding EU nationals' status and a meaningful vote on the final deal, though they have pledged not to frustrate the Brexit process itself. As the Commons debates the legislation, Labour leadership is managing internal divisions, including criticism of Shadow Home Secretary Diane Abbott for missing the previous vote, while attempting to negotiate compromises with the government.

Exeter City manager Kevin Nicholson confirmed that the club will receive a portion of midfielder Ryan O'Kane's transfer fee to the Cherries, due to a 15% sell-on clause from his 2222 sale. Nicholson emphasized that the funds are critical for the cash-strapped club, which has faced significant financial challenges after its previous owner departed. The Gulls are currently seeking new ownership and have been forced to drastically cut their playing budget and close their academy.

The inquest for Iwan Wyn Lewis, a patient who died in the Menai Strait, heard that a police visit regarding his bail arrangements caused distress and agitation, potentially contributing to his death. Consultant psychiatrist Dr. Olufemi Adebajo criticized the unapproved visit, stating it likely increased Lewis's distress. Lewis had previously reported feeling agitated and requested extra medication, but staff did not adjust his dosage before he was found dead in the strait. The inquest into the circumstances surrounding his death is ongoing.

Sheffield Wednesday signed forward Taylor-Fletcher from Leicester City, prior to their match against Norwich City. The 33-year-old has been limited to just two appearances for Leicester this season despite signing a new one-year deal in the summer.

US scientists are storing climate data on servers outside of federal control, fearing that the Trump administration will restrict access to research due to its skepticism of global warming. Dr. Waleed Abdalati argues that maintaining public access to taxpayer-funded data is in everyone's best interest, while other researchers warn that history may repeat itself if the administration curas scientific information.

John "Brad" Bradbury, the drummer for the ska band The Specials, has died at the age of 69, following the recent death of band trombonist Rico Rodriguez. The band announced his passing on social media, paying tribute to him as a "world's greatest drummer" and a key figure in the Two Tone sound. The cause of death was not disclosed, but his family issued a statement honoring his groundbreaking contributions to music and his integral role in the band's history.

Tiger Woods missed the cut at the PGA Tour event at Torrey Pines, finishing four shots behind the cut line despite a level-par second round. World number one Jason Day, US Open champion Dustin Johnson, and overnight leader Justin Rose also failed to advance, while Rose took the lead on eight under par. Woods, playing in his first full event in nearly 18 months, expressed frustration at missing a chance to win but noted significant improvement in his ball-striking and putting compared to his first round.

Former footballer Chris Cole, undergoing treatment for kidney failure, has returned to his role as Manchester United ambassador but is still recovering from his illness. He underwent a transplant using a kidney from his nephew and is now focusing on physical recovery, with hopes of participating in future matches. Additionally, Cole expressed skepticism about English clubs' ability to compete for the Champions League, noting they are significantly behind top European teams.

Pakistan has lifted its ban on YouTube after Google launched a local version that allows authorities to request the removal of content deemed illegal within the country. While the government and many citizens have welcomed the restoration of access, activists are calling for greater transparency regarding the specific terms of the agreement between Google and the state. YouTube maintains that it will only restrict content after a thorough review and in accordance with its community guidelines.

Leicester director of rugby Richard Cockerill confirmed that 26-year-old player Benjamin will likely miss the rest of the season after sustaining an injury in last week's victory over Exeter. Meanwhile, scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract, though the specific terms were not disclosed. Cockerill assured fans that Benjamin’s injury is not serious and he is expected to make a full recovery within eight to ten weeks.

Ethan Doull helped Great Britain’s men's team pursuit squad win Olympic gold in world record time, to emulate fellow Welsh champion Geraint Thomas. Doull, who had previously won silver medals at the World Championships, described the victory as a "surreal" culmination of four years of hard work and a moment of Olympic redemption.

The death toll from severe flooding in India has doubled to over 100, as officials discovered more bodies when waters receded, affecting approximately 450,000 people in the state. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Assam to address the recurring crisis, which has impacted millions across at least 20 states this monsoon season. The government has announced aid packages for the affected regions, while some residents in Gujarat have begun returning to their villages.

Bridget and Jonathan Reid, from the Scottish Highlands, married at Nevis Range in full wedding attire before skiing down the slopes. The couple, who began their relationship with a skiing trip six years ago, utilized recent snowfall to host their unique ceremony at the top of Easy Gully. They described the event as a perfect day with excellent conditions, thanks to the support of the resort staff and an adventure photographer who captured the moment.

Hong Kong regulators imposed a fine on RBS due to serious inadequate controls that allow former trader Shirlina Tsang to falsify emerging markets trade records, resulting in her 50-month prison sentence. The fine was reduced because the bank promptly alerted authorities and implemented a comprehensive remediation program. This penalty is significantly lower than other recent fines RBS has paid, including hundreds of millions for Libor rigging and US sanctions violations.

Backstage at the BAFTAs, winners such as Tom Holland and Viola Davis and Casey Affleck were sharing their reactions to recent entertainment news. Holland, who won the Rising Star Award, joked about the physical toll of playing Spider-Man, while Davis defended Meryl Streep against political criticism and Affleck praised her Golden Globes speech.

World number one Andy Murray’s 2017 season has been plagued by injuries, including shingles and an hip problem, which his recent loss to Jordan Thompson at Queen's Club highlights. Murray’s physical condition remains uncertain as he prepares for Wimbledon, with reports indicating that he is currently walking with a limp and struggling with his movement. While Murray has a strong historical record at the All England Club, his current form and fitness levels suggest he may face significant challenges in defending his title.

South African DJ Mandla Hlatshwayo was fatally shot in Soweto while attempting to stop a group of men who had robbed women of their mobile phones. Police have arrested suspects in possession of drugs and an unlicensed gun, and are currently questioning them to link them to the crime. Tributes have poured in for the 40-year-old, who was remembered by friends and colleagues as a selfless man.

Merseyside Police are investigating a shooting near Anfield Road Primary School, which occurred around 09:00 GMT, but authorities confirmed that no injuries were reported. While schools in the area remain on lockdown during the investigation, staff confirmed that students are safe and classes are continuing as normal. Police are currently reviewing CCTV and conducting house inquiries to identify a suspect described as a white man in a grey hooded top who fired at a dark-colored car.

Olympic champion Jessica Ennis-Hill sits third overall after a strong first day of the heptathlon, needing 6,200 points to qualify for the Rio Olympics. Canada's Brianne Theisen-Eaton currently leads the competition with 5,834 points. Ennis-Hill remains on course for qualification despite a disappointing javelin throw, with the final 800m event yet to be completed.

Manor Racing has officially ceased operations after its administrator, Just Racing Services, failed to find a buyer, resulting in the immediate redundancy of all staff. The team's collapse reduces the Formula One grid to 10 teams for the upcoming season opener in Australia, raising concerns about the financial sustainability of smaller teams under the current prize money distribution system.

Manor's failure has prompted calls for a European Commission investigation into the sport's governing bodies, with critics arguing that the current financial structure unfairly favors larger teams and contributes to the instability of smaller entrers.

The upcoming Stormont election on 2 March will return 90 members, down from 108 in previous polls, featuring 70 female candidates among 228 total contenders. The Democratic Union Party (DUP) is fielding the largest number of candidates with 38, followed by Sinn Féin with 34. West Tyrone, East Londonderry, and East Antrim have the highest number of candidates at 15 each, while Newry and Armagh has the fewest with nine.

Anthony Reuben from BBC Reality Check advises Drew, who is planning a trip to New York in December, that the exchange rate between the pound and the dollar reflects investor views on the relative strengths of the two economies. Since the Brexit vote, the pound has fallen approximately 18% against the dollar, driven by expectations of stronger US growth and lower UK interest rates. Reuben suggests that Drew could "hedge his bets" by buying half of his dollars now and the rest closer to his trip, while also recommending that he shop around online for the best rates rather than buying at the airport.

19-year-old Zoe Waters, a Newcastle University student, was named the winner of the Alternative Model of the Year competition, which attracted over 300 entrers. Waters, who describes herself as "crazy" in her fashion choices, expressed shock at her victory and stated her intention to pursue a career in alternative modeling. Organizers highlighted the event as a celebration of subcultures, aiming to counter prejudice by showcasing diverse styles and identities.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy has proposed moving the "Yomper" statue from Eastney to Portsmouth, as part of a £13m project to relocate the Royal Marines Museum, sparking opposition from local campaigners. The statue, which depicts a Royal Marine from the 1882 conflict, has been a local landmark since 1992 and is viewed by supporters as a vital part of Eastney's heritage. Museum officials argue the move would expose the statue to significantly more visitors, while opponents insist it belongs in its original outdoor setting.

A suspect, known only as BM, has appeared at the Old Bailey charged with the first alleged breach of Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPims), failing to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January. The Home Office declined to comment on the specific case, confirming that police investigate and prosecute viable breaches of these orders. BM was granted unconditional bail but remains subject to the restrictions of his TPim while awaiting a trial date.

Seamer Anyon has been appointed as the new women's cricket coach at Sussex, taking over from Charlotte Burton and also overseeing the under-19 and under-21 teams. Anyon, who retired last year due to a knee injury, expressed his excitement about contributing his professional experience to the rapidly growing women's game. Additionally, Alexia Walker has been assigned to coach the senior, under-21, and under-19 sides.

Wes Brown's 23-year-old brother, who previously on trial with Shakers, has officially signed with Bury and is available for their League One season opener against Doncaster. The player, who has made over 50 Football League appearances for various clubs including Bradford, Doncaster, and Oldham, is now eligible to play for Bury this Saturday.

Kenneth Branagh’s live-action adaptation of *Cinderella* has grossed $70 million on its opening weekend in the US, despite being a strictly faithful retelling of the traditional fairy tale.

The film’s success is attributed to its classic approach, which director Branagh argues allows the original story’s deeper psychological themes to resonate more effectively than modernized versions. While some critics view the film's lack of gimmicks as charmingly old-fashioned, the cast emphasizes that this Cinderella is defined by her own choices and courage rather than passive waiting.

Ukraine banned Russian singer Julia Samoilova from the Eurovision Song Contest because she performed in Crimea, which Ukraine considers illegally annexed by Russia, in violation of its border laws. The European Broadcasting Union attempted to resolve the dispute by offering Russia a satellite broadcast option, but Moscow declined and chose to boycott the event entirely. This unprecedented exclusion highlights the deep political tensions between the two nations, turning the music festival into another battleground for their ongoing conflict.

Alex McKechnie, a regular attendee at The Cavern Club during the early Beatles' residency, recalls the intimate and energetic atmosphere of the small basement venue where the band performed 292 times. He describes the group as a "complete package" with strong harmonies and a rebellious, charismatic stage presence that defied the polished styles of their contemporaries. McKechnie emphasizes that the Beatles' early identity was defined by their irreverence toward authority and their ability to captivate a small, highly charged audience with their adventurous sound.

South Africa’s government has proposed a minimum wage to combat income poverty, while critics warn that the rate could potentially increase unemployment because employers might not be able to afford higher labor costs. The proposed figure has drawn mixed reactions, with some experts arguing it is insufficient to sustain a household while political parties debate its impact on business versus workers. The government aims to finalize the national minimum wage within two years, despite ongoing concerns about economic stability and credit ratings.

The death of Ethiopian leader Meles Zenawi has heightened concerns about a potential power struggle in Addis Ababa, which could destabilize the Horn of Africa region amidst ongoing political crises in Somalia and Sudan.

Meles is remembered as a complex and influential figure who transformed Ethiopia through economic modernization and infrastructure development, though his legacy remains contested due to his increasingly autocratic rule and failure to address systemic poverty and political repression.

Australia dominated Pakistan's first day of the second Test at the MCG, taking wickets at regular intervals despite rain limiting play to just 50.5 overs. Asif Ali scored a crucial 110-ball half-century, surpassing 1,000 Test runs for the year. The hosts maintain a 1-0 lead in the three-Test series after their victory in the opener.

In a historic by-election for the Leith Walk ward, the SNP’s John Lewis Ritchie and Labour’s Marion Donaldson were elected using the Single Transferable Vote (STV system, marking the first time two members were selected in the same ward via this method. The SNP also retained the Midlothian West seat, while the turnout for both by-elections was recorded at 25.1%. These contests were triggered by the resignations of previous council members who secured parliamentary seats.

Amid escalating tensions, US Secretary of State John Kerry warned that Washington is "on the verge" of suspending military cooperation with Russia over Syria, after Moscow continued its air campaign against moderate opposition groups. The Russian government has defended its actions, arguing that the US has failed to sufficiently separate these groups from designated terrorists. Both nations remain engaged in diplomatic efforts, including potential talks in Geneva, while the humanitarian crisis in Aleppo intensifies with over 25000 civilians trapped under siege.

Wales has selected Llandovery hooker Hooker Hughes and Scarlets flanker Evans for their squad in the June Junior World Championship. The pair, who are both in their early twenties, will compete in Pool A against Ireland, Georgia, and New Zealand in Manchester. Scarlets general manager Jon Daniels praised their successful Six Nations campaign, noting that they will carry confidence into the upcoming tournament.

Amid escalating tensions, Russian officials, including Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev and Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova, strongly deny US allegations of election interference and condemn the Obama administration's sanctions as vindictive and baseless. Meanwhile, US officials justify the punitive measures by citing Russian intelligence activities and cyber-aggression, arguing that these actions aim to destabilize democracies globally rather than simply influence a specific election outcome.

Jeremy Corbyn proposes a complete abolition of university tuition fees in England, as part of a bold "all-or-nothing" strategy aimed at appealing to younger voters and ensuring education is not detered by cost. The plan, which also reinstates maintenance grants, is estimated to cost £11.2bn annually, though independent analysts suggest the true expense to the Treasury may be lower. This shift marks a significant departure from previous Labour policies, effectively dismanting the current system of loans and repayments in favor of direct government funding for universities.

West Sussex Fire and Rescue Service has concluded their recovery operation at the site of the Shoreham Air Show tragedy, where a vintage jet crash killed eleven people, Chief Fire Officer Sean Ruth praised the overwhelming public support received during the weeks-long effort. Meanwhile, Sussex Police have finished their work at the scene, though their investigation into the cause of the crash continues. The Air Accidents Investigation Branch is now seeking to interview the pilot, Andy Hill, as authorities prepare to reopen the affected section of the A27.

Intelligence chiefs Dan Coats and Mike Rogers refused to discuss their private conversations with President Trump during a public Senate hearing, citing national security protections, while both insisted they had never been directed to act illegally. The testimony frustrated senators who were pressing for details regarding allegations that the president attempted to derail the Russia investigation. Former FBI Director James Comey’s upcoming closed session is expected to provide more substantive answers than the current public hearing.

White House spokesman Josh Earnest confirmed that a private party was held on Saturday, but he did not elaborated further regarding the details. The event was reportedly attended by 500 guests, including lobbyists, CEOs, and celebrities such as Prince and Stevie Wonder. The Obamas paid for the party out of their own pocket, though the total cost was not disclosed.

 Therefore, there is no news story to summarize, and no specific event or context can be derived from this data.

In a BBC One episode, Dr Rangan Gleeson demonstrates how dietary changes can significantly alleviate symptoms of anxiety, depression and panic attacks by shifting a patient's diet from processed foods to fresh, whole ingredients. The article highlights growing scientific evidence, including a landmark Lancet study, that nutrition plays a critical role in mental health, arguing that doctors must better integrate dietary advice into patient care. Emma, the patient featured, reported improved mood, reduced panic attacks and greater mental resilience after adopting a healthier lifestyle.

The Alabama Securities Commission concluded its investigation into the publication of Harper Lee's new book, *Go Set a Watchman*, without finding any fraud, stating that the 88-year author was capable of consenting to the release. Despite the investigation's closure, some critics still suggested that Lee was manipulated into publishing the decades-old manuscript, which features characters from her famous novel *To Kill a Mockingbird*. Lee's lawyer defended the author, stating she was "extremely hurt" by the allegations of coercion.

The United States has suspended its participation in bilateral talks with Russia regarding the Syrian ceasefire, accusing Moscow and the Syrian government of failing to stop their intensified aerial bombardment of Aleppo.

 Russia rejected these accusations, arguing that Washington is shifting blame for the collapse of the truce and failing to distinguish between moderate opposition groups and jihadists. Despite the suspension of broader negotiations, both nations agreed to maintain limited communication regarding counter-terrorism operations to prevent accidental clashes.

Sadiq Khan’s election as London's first Muslim mayor has received international congratulations from political figures and media outlets, who hailing his victory as a symbol of liberal tolerance and successful integration. The global press has framed the win as a significant counter-narr to rising right-wing populism in Europe, highlighting Khan's background as a model for immigrants and Muslims across the continent.

St Paul's Church in Shipley turned to social media and a catchy song composed by children to find a vicar after traditional advertisements failed to attract applicants. The viral video, which garnered over 300 views and significant media attention, outlined quirky requirements such as a cheerful disposition and a love for Harry Potter. The church has now successfully appointed its new vicar, Henriette Howarth, who is set to start next week.

Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne will be sidelined for approximately 10 weeks after suffering a serious injury during the match against Everton, which he scored in. The Belgian international is expected to miss up to 13 games, including key fixtures in the League Cup final and the Champions League, while Everton goalkeeper Joel Robles has publicly apologized for his reaction during the incident.

A 27-year-old Swiss man died after setting fire to a train and stabbing passengers in Switzerland, resulting in six injuries including the attacker. Police currently have no indication of a political or terrorist motive and believe the man acted alone, as forensic experts analyze the scene and the flammable liquid used in the attack.

Devon and Cornwall Police are investigating after a drone flew dangerously within 2 miles of a Flybe passenger aircraft approaching Newquay Airport, causing a near miss with 62 people on board. The incident occurred when the drone entered the air traffic zone without Air Traffic Control clearance, prompting authorities to label the operator's actions as a "complete disregard for public safety." Police are appealing for public assistance to identify the reckless drone operator, who violated strict flying regulations regarding proximity to aircraft.

A grey seal was rescued from Cruden Bay by the Scottish SPCA, whose officers cut free a large fishing net that had been tangled around its neck. The seal was treated at the charity's rescue centre in Drumoak and was successfully released back into the water without suffering any injuries.

The National Library of Scotland has completed a year-long cataloguing of the extensive archive of travel writer and war hero Sir Patrick Leigh Fermor, comprising 16 metres of shelving filled with letters, manuscripts, and notebooks. The collection highlights his dual legacy as a celebrated author, with prized items including his 1933 European trek notebook, and a World War II veteran who led a daring operation to capture a German commander on Crete. Library staff are now working to digitize the materials and plan exhibitions to make this history of his "colourful life" accessible to the public.

Mr Roache has been elected as the new general secretary of the GMB union, defeating rival Paul McCarthy with 56.7% of the vote. He succeeds outgoing leader Paul Kenny, who stepped down after nearly a decade, and has pledged to lead a modern union focused on fighting for members' interests. The GMB, the UK's third largest union with over 600,000 members, remains a significant financial affiliate of the Labour Party.

Singer Laura Mhla is preparing for the release of her second album, *The Dreaming Room*, and her upcoming live television performance on *Later... with Jools Holland*, despite her well-documented stage fright. Mhla expresses excitement for the project but admits to being terrified of the high-pressure environment of live TV. However, she finds comfort in the show's reputation for genuine artistic interaction, viewing it as a special and respected platform in the music industry.

Newcastle United player Jonas Gutierrez has been returning to football after undergoing treatment for cancer, which he diagnosed in 22014. The 31-year-old Argentine revealed the emotional impact of his diagnosis and the support he received from teammates, stating that he feels "born again" and is focused on proving he can still compete in the Premier League.

Exeter City reported a £1.62m profit for 2014-15, driven by a record £1.7m transfer fee for midfielder Matt Grimes, despite facing cash flow issues that necessitated an emergency loan to pay player wages. The club has now secured planning permission to redevelop St James Park, with board members planning to reinvest the transfer income into improving the club's infrastructure. This financial turnaround marks a significant shift from the previous year's deficit and recent liquidity struggles.

Abdullah Hayayei, a 36-year-old Emirati para-athlete, died after a metal pole from the throwing cage collapsed on his head during training at Newham Leisure Centre in London. The Health and Safety Executive and police are currently investigating the incident. Hayayei’s vice president confirmed that the UAE team will continue competing in the World Para-athletics Championships to honor their teammate, who was preparing for the F34 class events.

A recent survey by the Scottish Chambers of Commerce indicates that many Scottish businesses are optimistic for 2017, despite recent official economic figures showing weakness in the broader economy. However, this optimism is tempered by significant challenges, including rising prices, skill shortages, and falling sales in key sectors like tourism and retail. Neil Amner, chairman of the economic advisory group, warns that while business mood remains positive, firms must manage costs and maintain consumer demand to navigate these pressures and international uncertainties.

The London inquiry into undercover policing has begun, as it is the first public examination of the tactics, which revealed that officers had relationships with women and used the names of dead children.

Helen Steel, who had a relationship with an undercover officer, said police committed "human rights abuses" and that the inquiry should expose both creditable and discreditable conduct, practice and management.

The home secretary ordered the review after claims police spied on the family of Stephen Lawrence, and the inquiry will report to the home secretary and make recommendations as to the deployment of undercover police officers in future.

The All Blacks survived a tough challenge against South Africa to advance to the World Cup final, despite trailing by five points at halftime with a player in the sin-bin. Dan Carter’s drop-goal and Beauden Barrett’s try secured the narrow victory for New Zealand. The champions now stand as favorites to retain the Webb Ellis trophy after overcoming a resilient Springbok defense in a gritty, low-scoring match.

The National Trust has deployed ground-penetrating radar to investigate the Wellington Monument on the Blackdown Hills, aiming to identify voids and gaps within its stonework. The 174ft tower, built in 1817 to commemorate the Duke of Wellington, has been fenced off since 2005 due to falling stone debris. This data will help create a computer model to develop a more effective and sustainable repair approach for the historic landmark.

Inditex, the parent company of Zara, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €1.26bn and an 11% rise in sales, driven by strong online expansion and steady economic growth in Spain. The retailer highlighted its strategic investment in technology, including mobile payments and online store expansion, to seamlessly integrate digital and physical shopping experiences. This robust performance contrasts sharply with European rivals like H&M and Next, who have cited unseasonal weather for their disappointing results.

Lady Gaga is currently preparing for her Super Bowl performance, which will spanning her career, and she has been undergoing rigorous rehearsations in Hollywood studios. The article highlights some of the most memorable and surprising Super Bowl performances from the past 30 years, including Michael Jackson's iconic 90-minute pause, Bruce Springsteen's energetic crotch-slam, and Beyoncé's politically charged "Formation" performance.

A new BBC documentary, *The Betrayed Girls*, highlights the ongoing sexual exploitation of teenage girls by Asian men in Greater Manchester, featuring victim Laura’s testimony that she still faces harassment from such groups.

Former prosecutor Nazir Afzal warns that despite increased prosecutions, many victims are still not being listened to or told their cases are too difficult to pursue, urging for more proactive and collaborative efforts between police and support agencies.

Victoria Centre store is closed "until further notice" after a burst pipe caused significant water damage to stock and the interior. Staff are working around the clock to clean up the flood, which left the top floor under three inches of water, in an effort to reopen as soon as possible.

Three independent analyses detected a flood of over 400,000 automated comments to the Federal Communications Commission, which appear to have been generated by bots using stolen personal data to mimic genuine public submissions. The comments, which feature remarkably similar wording and suspicious posting patterns, were likely created to influence the ongoing net neutrality debate. experts warn that this artificial activity muddies the waters by creating a false impression of mixed public support for the FCC's proposals.

Sale Sharks director of rugby Steve Diamond has confirmed that the club is close to signing a new full-back, while winger Nick Scott is on trial, as the team aims to strengthen their backline for the upcoming season. This recruitment drive follows a strategic shift by chairman John Cotton, who has moved home games back to Friday nights and promised significant improvements to the fan experience following years of declining attendance since the club's move to the AJ Bell Stadium. Cotton emphasized his commitment to rebuilding the club into a strong competitor at the highest level, alongside a new board structure that includes rugby director Steve Diamond.

Disney's *Moana* earned an estimated $81.1 million on its Thanksgiving debut, making it the second-highest opening of all time, but it has faced criticism for cultural appropriation regarding its merchandise. *Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them* finished second with $65.8 million, while Brad Pitt’s *Allied* and Warren Beatty’s *Rules Don't Apply* rounded out the top four with modest earnings.

World number 18 Johanna Konta, the third seed, defeated American wildcard qualifier Sachia Vickery 6-3 6-1 in just over an hour, showcasing 11 aces in a comfortable victory. Konta will advance to the quarter-finals where she faces China's Saisai Zheng on Friday.
Two men were hospitalized after an attack occurred on Linn Road on Sunday afternoon. Police are appealing for witnesses to contact them with any information regarding the incident.

A scientific team investigating the source of the Ebola outbreak in Guinea’s Meliandou village concluded that patient Emile’s infection likely occurred through exposure to infected bats in a hollow tree stump near his home. The study, published in EMBO Molecular Medicine, suggests that the bats’ droppings in the tree, rather than bushmeat consumption, triggered the rare transmission event. Researchers emphasize that while bats can carry the virus, culling them is not a viable solution due to their crucial role in controlling insect populations.

World number two Stuart Bingham has expressed his willingness to participate in the upcoming snook tournament, contingent on whether his wife gives birth before his first-round match. The 39-year-old champion stated that he and his wife are discussing the situation, noting that her previous labor experiences suggest there may be enough time for him to play if the baby arrives. However, he humorously acknowledged that the baby might not be ready to emerge yet.

The council has voted to urgently dismantle a dangerous section of the Grade II listed pier, citing the risk of further collapse as grounds for bypassing standard conservation consent procedures. The emergency work is expected to take approximately three weeks, with up to £65000 allocated for the operation. While the exact final cost remains uncertain, officials have priorited public safety by saving and cataloging salvageable parts of the structure that had already been closed to the public.

The Campaign to Protect Rural England (CPRE) will challenging the Castle Mill development in Oxford to the High Court, arguing that the city council failed to conduct an environmental impact assessment. He emphasizes the critical need for a political solution that incentivizes Sunni Arabs to support the Iraqi government rather than oppose it. Petraeus views the recent loss of Ramadi as a significant strategic setback but remains confident that the territory can be retated, provided that both political and military strategies are effectively aligned.

The City of Edinburgh Council has confirmed that its website service provider in England was targeted by hackers ten days ago, resulting in the compromise of only email addresses. officials have reported the incident to the Information Commissioner and the UK Government's Computer Emergency Response Team, while warning affected individuals to be vigilant against potential spam or phishing emails. The council has implemented additional security measures and is actively contacting those impacted to offer support and reassurance regarding the safety of their remaining personal data.

Syrian rebel groups declared a renewed offensive in Aleppo and Hama provinces, responding to regime attacks on residential areas, while the Syrian opposition delegation in Geneva announced its intention to suspend formal peace talks. The escalation of violence threatens to collapse the US-Russia-brokered cessation of hostilities, which had previously reduced fighting since late February. US officials have called on Russia to use its influence to halt the attacks and save the fragile diplomatic process.

Instagram, which owned by Facebook, will introduce ads in a few months to fund its future and make the platform a sustainable business. The social photo-sharing app has 150 million users but has never made a profit, despite its popularity among consumers. The company has learned from past backlash and assured users that they still own their photos, even as it enters the booming social media advertising market.

Michael Hall, known for his roles in *Dexter* and *Six Feet Under*, will perform David Bowie’s "Blackstar" at the 2016 Hyundai Mercury Music Prize ceremony. Radiohead leads the nominations with five previous wins, while other contenders include Laura Mvula and The 1975. The winner will be determined by a public vote that reduces the field to six finalists, followed by a decision by a judging panel. The event will be broadcast live on BBC Four and covered extensively on BBC Music News.

Gurpal Virdi, a retired Metropolitan Police detective, was acquitted by a jury at Southwark Crown Court on charges of indecently assaulting a prisoner and misconduct in public office. Virdi, who retired in 212 after 30 years of service, argued that the prosecution was part of a long-standing campaign to discredit him following his testimony regarding racism within the force. The charges, dating back to 1986, were dismissed after he presented evidence of alleged harassment and surveillance by the police department.

Welsh Secretary Alain Cairns and former MP Stephen Crabb are urging the UK government to adopt a more flexible Brexit approach, including maintaining access to the single market, to secure cross-party consensus. They argue that remaining in the single market is unnecessary given that both major UK political parties have voted to leave. However, other Conservative MPs, such as Simon Hart, have pushed back against this view, insisting that the election result does not invalidate the current Brexit strategy. Meanwhile, the Welsh Government has begun engaging in the Brexit process, emphasizing the importance of having a voice in the negotiations.

Hillsborough families have urged Home Secretary Theresa May to introduce a "Hillsborough Law" that would impose stricter obligations on public officials to cooperate with investigations, during private meetings in Warrington following the inquests. The relatives also expressed frustration over the conduct of South Yorkshire Police and demanded assurances regarding potential criminal prosecutions. Meanwhile, the Independent Police Complaints Commission has referred evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service, aiming to determine whether any officers should be charged by the end of the year.

The Crown Prosecution Service has issued new guidance stating that online harassment, including virtual mobbing and doxxing, will be prosecuted as if it occurred offline, while emphasizing that this does not infringe on free speech. The director stressed that context matters and that prosecutors will exercise caution when charging those posting "grossly offensive" material. The guidance aims to help police identify online crimes more easily, as victims of severe cyber abuse argue that current laws are insufficient to protect them from relentless harassment.

Faizan, a Kashmiri teenager, was fatally shot by paramilitary soldiers during violent protests against Indian rule at polling stations in Srinagar, which resulted in eight deaths and hundreds of injuries. The election, marked by a historic low voter turnout of 7.1%, was heavily boycoted by separatist groups and disillusioned citizens, dealing a significant political setback for mainstream parties. Eyewitnesses and videos suggest that soldiers fired into the crowds, leading to complaints being registered against the forces for their actions during the unrest.

A woman who was involved in a collision with a silver Ford Transit truck in Talysarn, Gwynedd, has died despite being flown to the hospital by air ambulance. North Wales Police are currently appealing for witnesses to the incident that occurred on Friday afternoon.

Four companies—Abellio, Arriva, KeolisAmey, and MTR—have submitted bids for the next Wales and Borders rail franchise, whose proposals are currently being assessed by Transport for Wales. The successful bidder, to be selected in early 208, will be required to reinvest any profits exceeding a negotiated cap back into the public transport system. This new model also mandates that the winner deliver a major upgrade to the rail network as part of the Metro scheme for south Wales.

Robbie Robinson, the 80-year-old broadcaster known as one of Scotland's most recognizable voices, is stepping down as permanent host of the long-running radio show *Take the Floor* after 35 years. BBC Scotland director Ken MacQuarrie praised Robinson for his decades of championing traditional Scottish music and the Doric dialect. First Minister Nicola Sturgeon also expressed her sadness at the departure, while Robinson confirmed that he will be handing over to a younger presenter but remains open to future one-off broadcasts.

Carlisle United manager Danny Stanley has publicly criticism the league's handling of his team's situation, arguing that they are an "unfair advantage" compared to Carlisle, who have been allowed to play three "home" fixtures at neutral venues following flooding. Stanley, whose own team has suffered two postponements due to waterlogging, believes the current arrangement is unfair to the other 23 teams in the league. He expressed sympathy for those affected by the weather but maintained that the rules are being shifted in Carlisle's favor.

Two supporters who cut themselves off from a stadium tour were found during a security sweep before an Arsenal game, but police decided not to arrest them. Manchester United confirmed that there was no risk to other attendees, noting that the pair had already passed through standard security checks. This incident follows a previous scare at Old Trafford six months ago involving a fake explosive device.

Accrington Stanley secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Preston North End in extra time thanks to Billy Kee’s stoppage-time winner. The match was end-to-end action with Jordan Hugill scoring twice for the visitors, before Ben Richards-Everton and Jordan Clark also finding the net for Stanley. The win continues Accrington’s recent success against higher-league opposition, following their victory over Burnley last season.

Andrew Bickel’s Facebook post about having his tools stolen and returned by a cat charity shop in Cardiff went viral, resulting in five minutes of fame for him. Bickel, who joked about appearing on *Judge Rinder and *I Love the Jungle, said he was glad no one was left out of pocket.

Scottish runner Eilid Muir will missing the Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast next year to focus on completing her final year of veterinary medicine studies. The 24-old athlete, who recently set a new outdoor personal best in the 5,000m, stated that her exams in May conflict with the April event, making her participation impossible. However, she remains optimistic about her future, potentially targeting the World Indoor Championships in March and looking ahead to multiple Olympic appearances.

Southend United manager Phil Brown expects jailed striker Nile Ranger to return to training before the season start, despite serving an eight-month prison sentence for online banking fraud. Brown plans to utilize behind-cclosed-door games to ensure Ranger achieves match fitness for the first League One fixture on 5 August. The club had previously stated they would consider the player's future following his guilty plea, but now appears focused on his potential return to the squad.

Veterer broadcaster Sir Terry Wintor has died of cancer at the age of 77, leaving behind a legacy of laughter and iconic radio shows spanning five decades. Tributes from colleagues, including Jeremy Vine and John Humphrys, as well as Prime Minister David Cameron, have praised his charm, wit, and ability to connect with audiences. A condolence book has been opened in London and his hometown of Limerick, where residents are encouraged to celebrate the life of "a true son of Limerick."

Unions at BAE Systems have warning of potential delays to the Royal Navy's new frigates, leading to concerns that up to 800 jobs could be lost if government commitments are not honored. Scottish political leaders are divided on the issue, with the SNP, Labour, and and the Lib Dems expressing deep concern over the uncertainty, while the Scottish Conservatives insist that the original timetable remains unchanged. The UK government and BAE Systems are currently working to finalize revised production schedules to address these concerns and protect the shipyards' future.

The Republican presidential debate focused heavily on immigration, healthcare, and Latino outreach, while candidates Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz united to aggressively attack front-runner Donald Trump on his business record and conservative credentials. Trump responded with personal insults, though he spent much of the evening on the defensive. The intense exchanges highlight the growing realization among his rivals that Trump is a formidable contender, even as they attempt to undermine his standing ahead of Super Tuesday.

Ukraine's Jamala won the Eurovision Song Contest with her song "1944," which focused the historical deportation of Crimean Tatars by Soviet troops, sparking debate over whether the victory was a result of musical merit or political messaging.

The win was widely seen as a symbolic rejection of Russia's Sergey Lazarev, who finished second, with many observers interpreting the result as a political statement regarding the ongoing conflict in Crimea. While some critics argued that the contest had become a political platform, others praised Jamala for her powerful performance and message of peace.

Rother District Council has allocated £51,000 to fund lifeguard patrols at Camber Sands, following eight recent drowning deaths that described as "significant and unprecedented." The service will operate from late May through the summer holidays to enhance visitor safety and support the local tourism economy.

Partick Thistle players, including captain Osman and Adam Barton, have publicly expressed their support to manager Archibald, urging the club to retain him despite his recent managerial shortlist appearances. The team praised Archibald for his consistent improvement of the squad and his strong relationship with the players. Meanwhile, the club is finalizing a transfer deal for promising centre-back Liam Lindsay, who is undergoing a medical at Barnsley.

Canadian authorities detained 10 individuals at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport, who all their passports confiscated, while investigations are ongoing. Police confirmed that none of the suspects have been charged yet, though their families have been informed and are currently dealing with the distress of the situation. Public Safety Minister Steven Blaney praised the officers' vigilance in protecting communities from the global terror threat, as Canadian troops continue their involvement in the coalition against IS militants.

21-year-old Dixon, who was captain of the Championship club's under-21 side, could make his debut for the Minstermen in Saturday's match against Newport. The Tigers player previously made his debut in the League Cup against Accrington Stanley in August.

The UK government aims to save £1bn annually from the NHS by targeting "health tourism" and recovering costs from foreign visitors, while implementing a levy on non-European temporary residents. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt argues that these measures are necessary to ensure the National Health Service remains a domestic rather than an international resource. The proposal has faced criticism from some medical professionals who question the accuracy of the financial estimates and express concern that the focus on eligibility checks could distract from patient care.

The Belfast Giants defeated Cardiff with a 5-1 victory, thanks to goals from Colin Shields, Scott Aarssen, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano. The win extends Belfast's lead in the standings, giving them a game in hand over the Devils. The Giants will face Manchester Storm on Wednesday, while Cardiff plays the Blaze on Tuesday as the busy festive schedule continues.

After undergoing significant restoration, a historic steam engine will make its first journey along the East Coast mainline in ten years. Originally built in Doncaster and named for its Edinburgh-to-London service, the locomette became a global icon of British engineering after the last original class member was withdrawn in 1666.

One out of five initial cases heard at the High Court in Leeds has been awarded compensation against the Catholic Church, while three other claims were dismissed. This legal action involves 249 men alleging historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school, where former staff members have already been jailed for their crimes. The De La Salle Brothers, who ran the school, have issued an unreserved apology for the abuse.
